captions.title: 10-year Treasury yield at 5.10%
captions.significance: The 10-year yield was 5.10% on 15 October, near its 5.31% high on 5 October; high long-term rates pressure long-duration technology valuations.

captions.title: High-yield credit spreads remain tight
captions.significance: High-yield spreads were 3.23% on 15 October, well below the 4.61% peak in April 2025, so the AI funding scare does not yet show broad credit stress.

captions.title: Micron falls 28% below June peak
captions.significance: Micron's adjusted price was $878.78 on 16 October, down 5.65% that day and 27.7% below its 25 June peak of $1,215.08, as CXMT's server-DRAM plan hit memory shares.

captions.title: CoreWeave falls 12% on AI debt fears
captions.significance: CoreWeave fell 11.89% to $61.40 on 16 October, 66.6% below its 20 June 2025 peak of $183.86; the drop is a direct sign of AI data-center credit and funding fear.

captions.title: Canadian Natural hits supplied-history high
captions.significance: CNQ rose 3.59% to $53.83 on 16 October, the highest in the supplied price history, while technology sold off; the move shows dated rotation into energy.

shared_review.critique_summary: Revised for causal precision and daily relevance. The draft's high-yield and Micron lines implied stronger causation than the evidence supports; I softened them. I also replaced the second Micron chart with an energy price chart to capture the rotation the brief highlights, while keeping Micron's latest operating income in the outline as fundamental context.

captions.title: High-yield credit spreads: stress is not broad yet
captions.significance: High-yield OAS was 3.23% on 15 October 2026, far below its 4.61% April 2025 peak; through that date, the spread did not point to general credit stress from AI.

captions.title: 10-year Treasury yield: still near 5%
captions.significance: The 10-year Treasury yield was 5.10% on 15 October 2026, down from 5.31% on 5 October but still near 5%, a continuing headwind for high-multiple technology shares.

captions.title: CoreWeave: equity gauge of AI funding stress
captions.significance: CoreWeave fell 11.89% to $61.395 on 16 October 2026, about 67% below its June 2025 peak, in a 10-13% drop across leveraged AI hosts; it is a live gauge of funding stress.

captions.title: Micron: memory supply fear versus record sales
captions.significance: Micron fell 5.65% to $878.78 on 16 October 2026, 28% below its June high, despite record $41.5bn quarterly revenue by 2026Q3; the gap is a de-rating on future memory supply.

captions.title: EOG Resources: energy rotation at a record
captions.significance: EOG rose 4.24% to $158.06 on 16 October 2026, a record in the series, matching the session's rotation into energy amid oil near $96 and a large US crude draw.

shared_review.critique_summary: The five-chart set is coherent: broad credit, rates, AI infrastructure, memory and energy. Revise the credit point so it does not imply the 15 October spread covers the 16 October equity session. CoreWeave is an equity gauge of funding stress, not a credit spread. Tighten Micron to separate reported revenue from the interpretation that future supply is driving the de-rating.
research_requests: Get 16 October high-yield OAS and CoreWeave credit default swap or bond yield levels to test whether AI-host stress spread after the equity selloff.
Track CXMT server DDR5 qualification and NAND contract prices to test whether future memory supply explains the Micron de-rating.
